verdict.rationale: ByteAsk documents its own sandbox modes: a `--sandbox workspace-write` flag, and a read-only run that can still build and run code under AddressSanitizer. Together these show the agent's file and tool actions run under a sandbox policy. The approval policy (`--ask-for-approval`) is a related control, not sandbox isolation, so it earns no credit here. The docs never describe what the sandbox actually isolates, and say nothing about network restrictions. Missing for 10: documented network-resource sandboxing, a description of the isolation boundaries and mechanism, sandbox coverage beyond the headless/exec docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can have the agent operate inside a sandbox when interacting with code, tools, and network resources

citations.quote: If you want the agent to build, test, or write files, pass `--sandbox workspace-write`.
A read-only run can still build your program under AddressSanitizer and run it.
